antonia

A woman sits calmly with her hands in her lap, painted in Modigliani's trademark style: a long neck, a simple oval face and almond-shaped eyes with no pupils. Modigliani was Jewish and was born in Italy, then lived in Paris. He painted friends and fellow artists over and over, and these quiet portraits have become some of the most recognizable faces in modern art.
portrait-of-paul-guillaume

A dapper art dealer in a hat sits with a confident, slightly sly look. Paul Guillaume was one of the first people to sell Modigliani's art, and Modigliani painted him more than once. The portrait shows how an artist could turn a friend and supporter into a stylish, graceful shape. It hangs in a museum in Paris.
portrait-of-moise-kiesling

Modigliani painted his friend, the painter Moïse Kisling, who was also Jewish and came from Kraków in Poland. The two artists lived and worked near each other in Paris and helped each other through poor times. The picture shows Kisling in warm tones and Modigliani's long, simple lines. It's a portrait of friendship between two outsiders who became part of the Paris art world.
chaim-soutine

Modigliani painted his friend Chaïm Soutine, a Jewish painter from a poor village in present-day Belarus. Soutine's own wild, swirling pictures were very different from this calm, simplified portrait. They shared a studio district in Paris, and Modigliani looked after him. Together they show how two very different styles could grow side by side.
self-portrait-amedeo-modigli

Modigliani looks out at us with the long face and narrow eyes he gave all his portrait subjects. Painted in the last year of his short life, it shows him as a quiet, thoughtful man. He died in Paris at only 35, but his fame grew enormously after his death. The painting hangs in a museum in Brazil.
ritratto-di-lunia-czechowska-con-ventaglio

A woman with a fan sits in a soft rose-and-brown room, painted with Modigliani's long curves. Lunia Czechowska was a friend and a favorite model in his last years. The elegant shapes make her look like a figure from a Renaissance painting. It's an example of his mature style.
tree-and-house

Modigliani is famous for portraits, but this rare landscape shows a small house and a tree in warm, simple colors. He painted it in 1919 in the south of France, where he went for his health. It is one of only a few landscapes he ever painted. It's a quiet glimpse of the artist outside his usual subjects.
the-banks-of-the-oise-near-pontoise

A tree-lined riverbank near Pontoise, a town northwest of Paris where Pissarro lived and painted. He helped teach Cézanne and Gauguin there, working outdoors with quick, fresh strokes. Pissarro was Jewish and born on a Caribbean island, and he was one of the founding fathers of Impressionism. His calm landscapes show the countryside he loved.
the-cote-des-bufs-pontoise

A hillside covered with orchards and small houses climbs above a village in the countryside near Paris. Pissarro painted the Côte des Bœufs hill many times, and Paul Cézanne later painted the same spot beside him. Painting the same place side by side taught both artists how to build a picture from color. It's a historic landscape of the early Impressionists.
the-house-of-the-deaf-woman-and-the-belfry-at-eragny

A cottage and a church belfry rise among trees in Éragny, the village where Pissarro lived for the last 20 years of his life. He painted in a pointillist way for a while, using tiny dots of color inspired by his young friend Seurat. The scene is peaceful and bright. It shows Pissarro experimenting even in his fifties.
shepherdess-bringing-sheep-in

A young woman guides her flock of sheep home at the end of the day, in soft golden light. Pissarro loved to paint country people at their work, because he felt the same dignity as in the lives of city people. He used small dots and dashes of color to make the light shimmer. It's a gentle image of rural life.
steamboats-in-the-port-of-rouen

Steamships and tugboats crowd a busy harbor in the French city of Rouen, with smoke rising into a hazy sky. Pissarro painted this from a high window when he was in his sixties. Rather than country fields, he now painted the bustle of modern ports and cities. It's a lively picture of industry and water.
morning-an-overcast-day-rouen

A bridge and the river in Rouen are wrapped in gray morning mist, with boats and buildings in soft shades of silver. Pissarro painted Rouen from hotel windows in the 1890s. The scene shows how he could make an ordinary cloudy day beautiful. It's one of his many city views from his last years.
boulevard-montmartre-mardi-gras

A busy Paris boulevard filled with crowds celebrates Mardi Gras, a festival before Lent, under bright flags and hazy light. Pissarro painted it from a hotel window above the street. The people look like tiny dabs of color, bustling along. It's an exciting snapshot of Paris in 1897.
rue-saint-honore-in-the-afternoon-effect-of-rain

Umbrellas and carriages move along a wet Paris street, with the buildings glistening in the rain. Pissarro painted this scene from a window, with a view of the shining pavement and the gray sky. The reflections make the picture glimmer. It is one of the most admired of his late city paintings.
boulevard-montmartre-spring

A wide Paris boulevard in spring sunshine is lined with trees in new leaf and busy with walkers and horse-drawn carriages. Pissarro painted a whole series of this boulevard in different seasons and weather. This one is bright and fresh. Together they show how one place can change all year.
landscape-with-character

A small figure stands in a swirling, wind-blown landscape, painted with thick, twisting strokes. Chaïm Soutine, a Jewish artist from a poor village in Belarus, used paint to express strong feelings instead of copying nature. His landscapes seem to move and twist like they are alive. He painted this in the south of France.
self-portrait-by-chaim-soutine

Soutine looks out at us with a serious, uneasy face in thick, quick brushstrokes. He came from a very poor family in a Jewish village in Belarus and was often ill and shy. His self-portraits are bold and emotional. This one is a powerful look at how an artist saw himself.
the-houses

Houses seem to lean and tumble down a hillside, painted in wavy lines and rich color, as if the earth was shaking. Soutine painted this in the village of Céret in southern France. The buildings seem to dance. It's a dramatic and unforgettable landscape.
the-idiot

A young man with a tilted head and a dazed face is dressed in blue, painted in thick, twisting strokes. Soutine painted many portraits of kitchen workers and ordinary people, and his pictures are full of emotion. The strange title reflects an old and unkind way of describing a person who seemed different. The painting asks us to look carefully at someone others might overlook.
portrait-of-a-man-emile-lejeune

A man in a dark jacket with a long face sits against a swirly background, painted with thick brushstrokes. Soutine painted this portrait in the early 1920s, before he became famous. The strong colors and lively shapes show how he used paint to express feeling. It's a typical example of his unique style.
the-little-pastry-cook

A boy in a white cook's uniform sits stiffly with his hands in his lap, painted in thick white and blue strokes. Soutine painted waiters, cooks and bellboys in Paris, with strong, emotional style. The wavy lines make the white clothes look almost alive. It's one of his best-known portraits.
still-life-with-rayfish

A large rayfish hangs against a dark background with a bowl and bottles, painted with wild, swirling strokes. Soutine was inspired by famous Dutch still lifes of fish and meat but gave them a more emotional twist. The fish seems to swim in the air. It's among his famous still lifes.
the-floor-waiter

A waiter in a white uniform stands stiff and serious with his arms at his sides. Soutine painted many hotel workers in Paris, with bold white uniforms in swirling paint. The unusual style makes the plain subject seem important. It's a well-known late portrait.
portrait-of-madeleine-castaing

A fashionable woman in a red dress sits in a chair against a swirling background. Madeleine Castaing was a Paris patron and collector who supported Soutine and bought many of his works. Soutine painted her in bold colors with a lively brush. It's a portrait of a friend who helped him succeed.
jews-mourning-in-exile

Jewish figures sit and stand by a riverbank, hanging their harps in the trees, in a scene based on a Bible psalm about mourning for Jerusalem during exile in Babylon. Eduard Bendemann, a German painter of Jewish background, painted it in 1832, when he was 21. It was a huge success and made him famous. It's one of the best-known Jewish subjects in 19th-century German painting.
two-girls-at-the-well

Two young girls in simple dresses gather water at a well in a calm landscape. Eduard Bendemann was a German painter from a Jewish family in Berlin who became a respected professor in Düsseldorf. He painted both Bible scenes and everyday life with soft, polished detail. It's a gentle, charming country scene.
portrait-of-lida-bendemann

A young woman looks thoughtfully out of the canvas in a quiet, warm portrait. Lida Bendemann was the artist's own relative, painted with careful detail. Eduard Bendemann was a leading German painter. It is a tender portrait of a family member.
an-allegorical-wedding-sketch-for-a-carpet-dedicated-to

A colorful design for a carpet, with symbolic figures celebrating a marriage. Ephraim Moses Lilien was a Jewish artist from Galicia, then part of Austria, who designed books, posters and carpets. He was an early artist of the Zionist movement and mixed Art Nouveau style with Jewish themes. It's a good example of how he brought together beauty and tradition.
portrait-of-a-wounded-knil-soldier

A wounded soldier of the Dutch colonial army sits quietly with bandages. Isaac Israëls was a Dutch painter from a Jewish family, and the son of the famous painter Jozef Israëls. He painted this early in his career. It shows his interest in real people, even in sad moments.
two-girls-in-the-snow

Two girls in warm winter clothes walk through a snowy street, looking out from under their hats. Isaac Israëls, a Dutch Impressionist, loved painting city people in motion. The quick brushwork makes the snow and the figures feel fresh. It's a charming winter moment.
hattery-mars-on-the-nieuwendijk-in-amsterdam

A hat shop on a busy Amsterdam street, with the window full of hats and the crowd walking past. Isaac Israëls painted the lively life of Amsterdam, which made him a leading painter of the city. The scene is quick and bright. It's a snapshot of 1890s shopping.
two-maids-on-the-lijjnbaansgracht-in-amsterdam

Two maids stand and chat by a canal in Amsterdam, with brick houses and water behind. Isaac Israëls painted ordinary women and children in the city's streets. The bold, loose style is typical of the Amsterdam Impressionists. It's a lively scene of everyday work and conversation.
shop-window

People pause on the street to look at a shop window, with their reflections in the glass. Isaac Israëls loved scenes of city life, with its crowds and shops. The quick brushwork gives a sense of moving life. It's a modern city picture from the 1890s.
portrait-of-jacqueline-sandberg

A young woman with a dark hat, painted with confident, loose strokes. Isaac Israëls was known for lively portraits of friends and city people. The style is fresh, fast and modern. It captures her personality in a few strokes.
beach-scene-in-scheveningen

Visitors stroll and play on the sunny beach at Scheveningen, the seaside resort near The Hague, under a wide sky. Isaac Israëls painted the busy beach with light, quick strokes. The tiny figures and sparkling sand are very lively. It's a happy summer day by the North Sea.
moulin-de-la-galette

A crowded dance hall in Montmartre in Paris, full of dancing couples and bright lights. Isaac Israëls painted this famous dance garden, which was also painted by Renoir and Van Gogh. His version is quick and full of motion. It's a lively picture of Parisian nightlife.
two-models-epi-and-gertie-in-the-amsterdam-fashion-hous

Two fashion models in elegant dresses at a fashion house in Amsterdam, painted with quick, confident strokes. Isaac Israëls was fascinated by modern fashion and city life. He painted this when he was in his fifties. It's a stylish picture of the Jazz Age.
woman-before-sunflowers

A woman sits in front of a large bunch of sunflowers, in a bright, sunny style. Isaac Israëls painted many women in colorful dresses and loved flowers. The yellow sunflowers glow behind her. It's a joyful portrait.
fresh-wind-volga

Sailboats lean in a stiff wind on the wide Volga River, under a big sky of fast-moving clouds. Isaac Levitan, a Jewish painter who grew up poor in Moscow, was one of Russia's greatest landscape painters. He painted the Volga in 1885 and captured the feeling of wind and open space. It shows how he made simple scenes powerful.
birch-grove

Slender white birch trees stand in a sunny grove, with patches of light falling on the grass. Levitan, a Jewish artist and a hero of Russian landscape painting, painted the trees with glowing green and gold. Birches are a symbol of Russia. The painting is bright, peaceful and fresh.
by-the-pool

A quiet, shaded pool is surrounded by tall trees, reflecting the sky. Isaac Levitan painted peaceful, thoughtful landscapes of the Russian countryside. His quiet mood and his soft colors became very influential. It's a calm, dreamy scene.
courthouse-waiting-room

People wait quietly in a courthouse hall, looking tired and worried. Isidor Kaufmann was a Hungarian Jewish artist who painted Jewish life in Eastern Europe with warmth. This early work shows his talent for painting real people in everyday places. It reminds us how artists record everyday life.
lady-in-an-interior-the-artist-s-wife

A woman sits in a calm, cozy room, with soft light on her dress. Isidor Kaufmann painted his wife, who was a model for many of his pictures. He is best known for tender pictures of Jewish people in Eastern Europe, and this is a family portrait. It's a loving, quiet picture.
cityshtetl

A shtetl, a small Jewish town in Eastern Europe, is painted with colorful, geometric shapes. Issachar Ber Ryback was a Ukrainian-born Jewish artist who blended folk art with modern painting. He wanted to keep the memory of Jewish village life alive. It's a bright, modern picture of a vanished world.
passing-mother-s-grave

A man and his child walk by a grave, in a sad and quiet mood. Jozef Israëls was a Dutch painter of Jewish background, known as the leader of the Hague School. He painted poor families and fishermen with deep sympathy. It shows how art can show feelings of loss gently.
dreams

A girl sits with a faraway look in a simple room, lost in thought. Jozef Israëls was a famous Dutch painter who showed the lives of poor families and fisherfolk with respect. The soft, dim light is typical of his style. It's a gentle, thoughtful picture.
fishermen-carrying-a-drowned-man

Fishermen carry one of their own in from the shore, with the wind and the waves behind them. Jozef Israëls was inspired by the harsh lives of fishing families in the Netherlands. The picture is sorrowful and powerful. It reminds us of the danger of life at sea.
children-of-the-sea

Two children play at the water's edge in a Dutch fishing village, wearing simple clothes. Jozef Israëls spent summers in the fishing village of Zandvoort and painted its people. The soft light on the sand and sea is lovely. It's a charming and moving image of childhood by the sea.
as-one-gets-old

An elderly woman sits by a fire, resting in a plain room, with a quiet, tired face. Jozef Israëls loved to paint simple people with great dignity. The title comes from a Dutch saying about growing old. It's a thoughtful look at old age.
alone

A woman sits alone in a dim room, with her head bowed. Jozef Israëls was a master of painting the loneliness of poor, working people. The few colors and soft light create a deep mood. It's a moving painting from the Hague School.
after-dark

A family sits in a dark house, with a single lamp lighting their faces. Jozef Israëls painted the calm and warmth of simple lives in Dutch homes. The glow of the lamp is gentle. It's a cozy, quiet scene.
a-jewish-wedding

A Jewish wedding is celebrated by a crowd in a village, with the bride and groom under a canopy. Jozef Israëls was born in a Jewish family in the Netherlands and sometimes painted scenes of Jewish life in later years. The picture is full of lively faces and warm light. It's a joyful record of a tradition.
dinner

A table is set for a dinner party in a richly decorated room. Léon Bakst was a Jewish artist from Russia, best known for designing amazing costumes and sets for the Ballets Russes in Paris. His rich color and sense of theater changed stage design. This early work shows his taste for glamor.
autumn-vase

A vase of autumn flowers sits in a swirl of rich red and golden colors. Léon Bakst used bold, glowing colors that later made his stage designs famous around the world. This picture shows the same love of color in a simple flower vase. It's a colorful decorative picture.
